script.title: Why Mission-Driven Teams Need an AI Copilot
script.body: What if your nonprofit could spend less time on administration and more time delivering its mission? Too many program teams are buried in repeated reporting, planning, and outreach work. We're exploring ProgramLift AI, a human-supervised copilot concept to help teams turn existing program materials into reusable workflows and draft communications. The goal isn't to replace staff judgment. It's to give mission-driven people more time for the people they serve. What would you simplify first?

captions.text: Nonprofits don't need another tool that adds work. They need support that helps existing programs go further while keeping people in charge. script.title: Measure Staff Value, Not AI Hype
script.body: For nonprofits, 'we used AI 500 times' is not an impact metric. Ask: Did staff find the drafts useful? How many corrections were needed? Did the workflow protect privacy? Did it create more time for human service? Measure what improves the mission—not what makes the technology look impressive.

script.title: Invitation: Help Shape the First ProgramLift Pilot
script.body: What if your next program improvement started with one workflow instead of an entirely new platform? We're exploring ProgramLift AI with a simple principle: AI can draft, but your team decides. We're looking to learn from nonprofit leaders who manage workshops, volunteer teams, outreach, and reporting. Share the task your team repeats every week. We'll discuss whether it makes sense to design a small, human-reviewed pilot together. No grand promises—just a useful conversation.

follow_up_sequences.name: Respond to genuinely interested public commenters
follow_up_sequences.allowed_entry_condition: Contact asks for details or explicitly invites a follow-up; never scrape or auto-DM commenters.

steps.subject: Thanks for the thoughtful question
steps.message: Thanks for engaging with the post. Which workflow in your nonprofit program takes the most repeat effort right now?
steps.exit_if: No consent or no relevant interest

steps.subject: A helpful example, if useful
steps.message: Following up because you asked about {{workflow_name}}. Here's a short, fictional example of how an AI draft plus human review might work. Would a brief conversation be useful?
steps.exit_if: Declined or requested no further contact

steps.subject: Closing the loop
steps.message: No pressure to respond. If exploring a small, human-reviewed pilot becomes useful for your team, I'm happy to compare notes. I'll leave it here for now.
steps.exit_if: No response after this final permitted follow-up

follow_up_sequences.name: Follow up after an agreed discovery call
follow_up_sequences.allowed_entry_condition: A real discovery call was booked and the participant agreed to receive recap and next steps.

steps.subject: Our program workflow conversation
steps.message: Thanks for explaining {{organization_type}}'s process around {{workflow_name}}. My understanding: {{human_verified_summary}}. Please correct anything I missed.

steps.subject: A small pilot outline for review
steps.message: Based on our conversation, a possible 14-day test could focus on {{workflow_name}} using only approved non-sensitive inputs. Shall we review the scope together?

steps.subject: Would a next step help?
steps.message: Checking whether you'd like to continue exploring a small test. If timing isn't right, happy to pause here.

follow_up_sequences.name: Respond to a pilot request with next steps
follow_up_sequences.allowed_entry_condition: A nonprofit representative explicitly requests pilot details.

steps.subject: Exploring an AI workflow pilot
steps.message: Appreciate your interest. Could you share the one recurring, low-risk workflow you'd most like to improve, the staff reviewer, and your preferred timeframe?
steps.exit_if: Pilot involves unapproved sensitive data or consequential automated decisions

steps.subject: Clarifying the pilot scope
steps.message: Thanks for the context. We can sketch a small, human-reviewed example and agree on what success would mean. Would you prefer a short call?

lead_scenarios.inbound_message: Could this help us turn weekly workshop notes into a facilitator recap?
lead_scenarios.draft_ai_response: Potentially as a draft workflow. For this concept we'd start with approved, non-sensitive notes, create a recap draft, and have your facilitator verify it. Which sections are hardest to prepare?

lead_scenarios.inbound_message: What happens to sensitive client information in an AI tool?
lead_scenarios.draft_ai_response: We wouldn't use sensitive client records in this demo. For any potential pilot, we would define permitted inputs and safeguards before testing. The concept is not presented as certified for protected client data.

lead_scenarios.inbound_message: Our volunteer reminder process takes too much coordination. What would a small test look like?
lead_scenarios.draft_ai_response: Thanks for sharing the challenge. A possible first test could draft volunteer reminders from approved schedules, with a coordinator reviewing every message before sending. Could we discuss the process on a short call?

lead_scenarios.inbound_message: We run monthly cohorts and might want to explore facilitator preparation.
lead_scenarios.draft_ai_response: That sounds worth exploring. Which materials does your facilitation team repeat each cohort, and which would need careful staff verification? We'd welcome a discovery conversation if useful.

kpi_definitions.approved_content: Approved via a human review record; drafts never count
kpi_definitions.meaningful_public_conversation: A relevant two-way exchange about real nonprofit workflow needs, not likes or impressions
kpi_definitions.permission_based_conversation: A direct conversation initiated or consented to by the recipient
kpi_definitions.discovery_call_requested: Recipient explicitly asks for, or agrees to, a discovery call
kpi_definitions.qualified_pilot_candidate: Nonprofit meets the criteria in launch_targets

analysis_questions: What workflows were most often requested?
Did the content attract real nonprofit operators rather than general AI enthusiasts?
Which messages led to permission-based conversations?
What must be tested in a human-reviewed pilot before any product claims?
